about.text: A soft white fresh cheese of Central and Eastern Europe: milk is fermented and the whey is drained off, traditionally in hanging bags. Its fat runs from nil to about 23 %, and unlike German quark it is often made from whole milk.

how.text: Milk is soured with a starter (and sometimes a little pepsin) for about 8 hours until it forms a curd block, which is cut, warmed a little to drain and pressed. The sources opened do not name the starter species.

steps.note: Standardised to the wanted fat first, so whole milk can be used; classic acid-set curd is often from skimmed milk.
In the acid-rennet kind rennet (chymosin) or pepsin is added with the starter.

steps.name: drain
steps.note: Traditionally in free-hanging bags; industrially the curd block is cut with strings, then squeezed, cooled and packed.

processing.text: Species are not named. The acid-rennet kind adds rennet or pepsin with the starter; the curd is then cut, warmed to 40-45 °C and drained.

facts.v: Full-fat 19–23 %, classic 4–18 %, low-fat 1.8 %, fat-free (GOST R 52096-2003 as cited)
Milk split into skimmed milk and cream (50–55 % fat); fat-free tvorog is made from the skimmed milk by acid-rennet set and the cream is mixed back in
